prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1177; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a sideswipe that occurred while the insured was changing lanes. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will be routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the photographs submitted with the claim. They confirm several details of the scene and the position of the vehicles, though no independent witnesses have come forward to describe the collision.

Entry 3: Vehicle damage on the claimant's side is consistent with the impact described in the report. The estimate lines up with the damage pattern shown in the photos, and no earlier damage to the vehicle is known from our records.

Entry 4: Police report confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the collision. The driver is named on the policy, and nothing in the file suggests the damage occurred before the coverage period began.

Entry 5: Claimant reports a knee injury from the crash. The injury fits the type and force of the collision, and no prior injury to the same area is known from the claimant's history.

Entry 6: Claimant has given the same account of the collision in every conversation so far, including through counsel. Medical records show treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the claimant improved.

Entry 7: Recommend the file proceed to settlement review based on the documented damage, consistent medical treatment, and the policy being in force at the time of loss. Counsel to be advised of the reserve and next steps.
